key_facts: The Welsh Government has been working with higher education (HE) and further education (FE) institutions since September 2016 to assess the impact of Brexit.
Cardiff University conducted research that has superseded previous sector analyses, including reports on the impact of Brexit on the Welsh economy.
The Welsh Government has not yet released formal risk assessments for HE and FE sectors regarding Brexit.
The European transition team within Welsh Government coordinates efforts across departments to prepare for Brexit impacts.

The Welsh Government is concerned about the potential impact of a 'no deal' Brexit on the FE sector, particularly in sectors like farming, health and social care, construction, and hospitality and tourism.
Under a 'no deal' scenario, the Welsh Government expects that ESF funding will continue until 2020, but there are concerns about future funding.
The Welsh Government has allocated £3.5 million to the Global Wales initiative to support international recruitment and marketing for HE institutions.
The Welsh Government has committed to implementing the Diamond review proposals for HE funding.
The Welsh Government has made an additional £5 million available to HEFCW to mitigate the freeze in tuition fees and support postgraduate studies.
There is a concern among Welsh Government officials that the removal of the tuition fee grant for EU students has impacted recruitment, leading to a drop in EU student applications.
The Welsh Government has not yet received clarity from the Treasury on future funding for EU students.
The Welsh Government has engaged with FE colleges to understand their preparedness for Brexit, particularly in relation to apprenticeships and ESF funding.
The Welsh Government is concerned about the potential loss of multi-year European funding for HE and FE sectors, which affects planning and stability.
The Welsh Government has stated that they expect to maintain a level of funding for apprenticeships, assuming the UK government fulfills its commitments.
The Welsh Government has been working with the FE sector to align training with employer needs through regional skills partnerships.
The Welsh Government has expressed concerns about the impact of Brexit on the ability of HE institutions to charge international fees, depending on the outcome of negotiations.
The Welsh Government has not yet confirmed any specific actions to prevent Brexit from exacerbating the drop in EU student applications.
The Welsh Government has emphasized the importance of maintaining the current level of funding for HE and FE sectors, as promised during the Brexit referendum.
